title: Objects & Modeling: Key-Value Pairs & Property Access
description: Master JavaScript objects: key-value dictionary modeling, dot vs bracket property notation, dynamic key access, and composing nested data structures.

objectives.statement: Model real-world domain entities using object literal notation with string keys and typed values.
Access and mutate nested object properties accurately using dot and bracket notation.

content.title: Modeling Entities with Objects
content.hook: While arrays are great for ordered lists, real-world data is structured into named properties: a user has a name, email, and score. Objects let you model structured entities using key-value pairs.
content.context: An object is an unordered collection of key-value pairs created with curly braces {}. You can access properties using dot notation (user.name) or bracket notation (user['name']). Bracket notation is required when property names come from variables or contain special characters.
goals: Create objects using object literal syntax.
Distinguish dot notation from dynamic bracket notation.
Read and update properties inside nested objects and arrays.

content.title: Dot vs Bracket Notation
content.description: obj.prop evaluates the literal property name 'prop'. obj[expr] evaluates expr dynamically as a JavaScript expression/variable to determine the key at runtime.

content.prompt: What streak number will be printed to the console?
content.explanation: user.stats.streakDays accesses 5, increments it by 1 to 6, and prints 6.

feedback.correct: Spot on! The nested streakDays counter is incremented from 5 to 6.
feedback.incorrect: Drill into user -> stats -> streakDays (5), then add 1.

content.title: Model a Course Module Object
content.prompt: Create `const course` with properties: `id: 'mod-101'`, `title: 'JavaScript Basics'`, `completed: false`, and `topics: ['Variables', 'Functions']`. Then update `course.completed = true;` and push `'Objects'` to `course.topics`.
hints: Define const course = { id: 'mod-101', title: 'JavaScript Basics', completed: false, topics: ['Variables', 'Functions'] };

feedback.correct: Great work! You modeled an entity with properties and manipulated nested array state.
feedback.incorrect: Check that course has id, title, completed (true), and topics (containing 'Objects').

content.question: When MUST you use bracket notation `obj[prop]` instead of dot notation `obj.prop`?

options.text: When the property key is stored inside a variable or contains spaces / hyphens.
Whenever the value is a number.
Only when the object was declared with const.
Bracket notation is deprecated in modern JavaScript.

content.explanation: Dot notation requires valid static identifier names. Dynamic variable keys or keys with hyphens/spaces require bracket notation.

feedback.correct: Correct! Dynamic property keys stored in variables must be accessed via bracket notation.
feedback.incorrect: Remember that dynamic variable names require bracket notation to evaluate the variable.

content.title: Objects & Modeling Mastered
takeaways: Objects model real-world entities using key-value pairs ({ key: value }).
Use dot notation (obj.name) for static keys; use bracket notation (obj[key]) for dynamic variable lookups.
Compose nested structures (arrays of objects, objects with arrays) to represent complex application state.
